paper.title_en: Effect of uniform bond-charge order on longitudinal spin-susceptibility jump at a superconducting instability inside a magnetic phase
paper.abstract_en: A previous work [H. Yamase and M. Zafur, Phys. Rev. B \textbf{103}, 224527 (2021)] showed that the longitudinal spin susceptibility exhibits a jump when the superconductivity develops continuously inside a magnetic phase. That analysis employed a minimal model containing magnetic and superconducting interactions. However, in correlated-electron systems, both magnetic and bond-charge interactions originate from the same underlying spin-spin exchange interaction. We therefore extend the model by including the uniform bond-charge order to provide a more realistic description of the system. We find that the jump of the longitudinal spin susceptibility remains robust even in the presence of uniform bond-charge order, but the uniform bond-charge order quantitatively enhances the longitudinal spin susceptibility and the size of the jump at $T_c$.
